Metro Centre Mayhem

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Could your home's building plans be at risk?

Unique Selling Point:
Joburg's Historical Archives at risk affecting development of the built environment.

Summary:
Over 1 million building plans are at risk in the condement Metro Centre.

Further information:
In September 2023, the Metro Centre building was evacuated after a fire.
But for at least four years, the City of Joburg was aware the building was unfit for occupation.
In 2019, the city commissioned a report on the state of the building which was allegedly rejected
by the previous administration.
This report indicated the building was uninhabitable owing to several structural, mechanical and
electrical concerns.

The city was also issued with two notices by the department of labour regarding contravention
of occupational health and safety regulations.
All this was ignored.
This is no surprise. The JPC - a municipal entity, is responsible for managing publicly owned
properties in Johannesburg.
Helen Botes, has served as its CEO for 15 years and also holds the position of acting chief
operating officer for the City of Johannesburg.
Remember the Usisndiso building fire which took 76 lives? The Khampepe Commission Report
found that the JPC board must consider taking appropriate action against Botes for her total
disregard of managing the building despite being aware of its dire state.
In other words, mismanagement of Joburg buildings is habitual for the JPC.

Ironically, on vacating 4800 employees from the Metro Centre, the city didn’t give much
consideration to the historical archives housed within the building.
Approximately 1 million town and building plans have been left behind. Some have already been
destroyed by leaks in the building.
These buildings contain not only the history of building in Johannesburg but the unwritten social
history contained within.
A group of concerned architects - including Heather Dodd - have repeatedly raised their
concerns with the city but have received no response.
Presently, the archives are in a mess to say the least.
Some people who have sold their homes have had to have the plans redrawn at a cost of
anywhere up to and more than R 100 000.
Dodd Architects has Wits as a client and it is housed on a farm which extends all the way to
parts of the northern suburbs.
Her firm has had to re-measure and re-draw plans for some of these areas in order to proceed
with commissioned work.
However, these re-drawn plans would not include any alterations made to the buildings or
homes historically.
This means mid-construction key changes to the plans can be discovered delaying the project
thereby making it more expensive.
This story also highlights the importance of a move from “brown files” to digitization of the
archives - a project the city had began.
However, the machine broke and the existing scans had been of poor quality.

MNet Text Script - Metro Centre Mayhem

(Masa) Vital documents tumbling from shelves…

(Masa) Stacks of files piled on the floor, hidden in darkness.

(Masa) Welcome to the Johannesburg City archives.

(Masa) As the City of Joburg prepares to host the G20 summit in November, the state of its buildings and infrastructure have come into sharp focus. Suddenly it's time to clean up - which is ironic because the plans needed to rejuvenate the city - stored in the Metro Centre behind me - are in a state of absolute chaos.

Masa) We were sent these pictures and videos by a source. They show the shocking state of an archive held by the Joburg Municipality at the Metro Centre in Braamfontein.

(Sarah Wissler) I've been in them, in 2016/2017 it looked like this, exactly like this! Stuff strewn everywhere and it's no better than this now.

(Masa) We had to investigate.

(Masa) It’s just a few rooms in a building you’ve probably never visited. So why should you care? Well, you’d be surprised by the impact of this gross mismanagement - maybe even on you.

(Masa) This is a story about a government apparently unable to manage its paperwork. The impact is significant: costly delays and penalties for property owners … taxpayer money wasted … development stalled… a city on its knees.

(Masa) Until two years ago, the Metro Centre is where the city’s endless parade of mayors had offices, and it even hosted the Zondo Commission into State Capture. But for years it’s been left to deteriorate.

(Masa) We wanted to see the state of the Metro Centre archive for ourselves - but the City claims it’s unsafe. Instead we head to the Randburg Civic Centre - another building belonging to the Joburg Municipality - and in an equally alarming state.

(Masa) Sarah Wissler, from ActionSA, says the chaos here mirrors what we would have seen inside the Metro Centre - a situation she says has existed for over a decade. Both buildings are managed by the Johannesburg Property Company or JPC.

(Sarah Wissler) JPC is always saying they have no money. So I don't know where the money is going because nothing is being fixed.

(Masa) Faulty wiring, caving ceilings… one of the largest store rooms in permanent darkness…

(Sarah Wissler) Oh good Lord, there’s a dead rat right here! Oh!

(Masa) The Metro Centre was closed two years ago, although, by then, it’s reported there’d already been two fires. Thousands of employees were moved to expensive rented offices… but archive staff still work in the condemned space, amidst an estimated one million abandoned building plans.

(Masa) Every single legal building in Johannesburg should be recorded on detailed plans in the City’s archive.

(Heather Dodd) It would show what’s there. Where all the walls are, where all the plumbing is, where the electrics are, what the windows look like, where the fire services are, all of those things.

(Masa) They’re drawn up by professionals like architect Heather Dodd.

(Heather Dodd) You draw up a computer model of the building and then you put together a set of submission drawings which you then submit to Council.

(Masa) Proposed renovations to a building must be reflected on its existing plans, and approved by Council. And if you want to sell your house, by law you’re required to include complete building plans in the sale.

(Masa) But if they can’t be found - something highly likely in Joburg - professionals have to measure the entire building and draw the plans from scratch - at your cost.

(Heather Dodd) This is an apartment building in Illovo, where we did extensive measuring up of an existing building that took a week and a half on site measuring up.

(Masa) Alternative technologies - like scanning the building using sensors - are expensive.

(Heather Dodd) A building like that could be more than R 100,000 probably to scan a building.

(Masa) And, once your replacement plans are drawn up, Council has to approve them, a process that could take months.

(Theuns Van Brakel) These delays are similar to what we initially experienced when COVID forced us to close our businesses and send people home. This is the second COVID. And it is unfortunate that the urgency of getting the council process and the Council filing system to the modern standard of what it’s supposed to be is not that high on the agenda of the Council.

(Masa) Town planner, Theuns Van Brakel, struggles to hide his frustration. He’s feeling the impact of the delays first hand.

(Theuns Van Brakel) Developers then are left out to dry, what happens? They downscale their business. They over time develop a shortage of housing or commercial or office or industrial buildings.

(Theuns Van Brakel) The professional people are having to reduce their employees. They've got to take salary cuts just to survive.

(Masa) Meanwhile, council spends potentially hundreds of wasted hours examining and approving redrawn plans that already exist: hours paid for by you, the taxpayer.

(Masa) This is what an archive is supposed to look like. It’s almost clinical, not the dusty, old-school archive I’d expected. It’s clean, climate-controlled - and most importantly, organised.

(Masa) A world away from the Metro Centre.

(Gabriele Mohale)This is years of neglect. This has been a long way coming.

(Masa) Gabriele Mohale is an Archivist of Historical Papers at Wits University.

(Masa Kekana) Looking at how the Metro Center building has been dealt with and the archives there, how would you think that affects governance in the city of Joburg?

(Gabriele Mohale) They don't know what they have in terms of records, if they get inquiries, if they have to write reports, if they have to be accountable for mismanagement or this and that. Archives provide evidence to our activities.

(Masa) The Wits archive is well-lit, access controlled, and monitored by smoke detectors for early fire warning.

(Masa) Gabriele shows us how architectural drawings are meant to be stored.

(Gabriele Mohale) It’s a traditional way of storing large format items. These ones can be sourced anywhere these filing cabinets.

(Masa) We’re told digitizing the Metro Centre archives would be the best solution, but it would cost around R 35 million.

(Masa) Probably a worthwhile investment, though, as the plans currently rotting away in the Metro Centre, are vital not only for individual property owners but for constructing and upgrading public infrastructure - and cracking down on illegal building.

(Theuns Van Brakel) That is the base from which the council makes the judgment on if a property is legal or unlawful.

(Theuns Van Brakel) So there's serious implications for a property owner if we cannot measure what is legal and what is illegal.

(Masa) In other words, the City’s complete disregard for organising the archives, let alone digitising them, is sabotaging growth and development.

(Masa Kekana) I mean, if the city can't get something as simple as paperwork right, how does it then manage billions of Rands?

(Sarah Wissler) Yeah, that's why with the oversight committees, we've got a major challenge.

(Sarah Wissler) To be honest with you, there's got to be a major shift so that we can get this sorted out and nobody actually cares about how things are being done properly. It's a fight, it's a constant fight every day.

(Masa) The City admits the current storage conditions at the Randburg Civic Centre are far from ideal due to space constraints.

(Masa) And it says it’s initiated a digitization project for all records at the Metro Centre which will begin in the new financial year.

(Masa) In the interim, the JPC is in the process of identifying a suitable building to relocate the archives, so service delivery can resume.

(Theuns Van Brakel) Every time that there is a major happening in the city, let's take the now upcoming G20 meeting of international leaders. The City of Johannesburg then scrambles to address issues. It is unfortunate that the city every time waits for one of these events to force them into action and therefore, it cannot be a once in a while fixer-upper, putting up some plasters to address problems. It cannot be done purely for window dressing for a short time.

(Masa) Generations of mayors have promised to revamp the Metro Centre - and the latest budget is a whopping R800 million. As the building deteriorates, so do the archives - and the city around them.
